children: Australia's manufacturing sector contracted in September 2026 for the first time in six months, led by a sharp drop in factory output and weakening order books, according to preliminary private survey data.

The S&P Global Australia Manufacturing PMI fell to 49.3 in September from 52.0 in August. Manufacturing output dropped to 46.4 from 49.6, marking its steepest monthly decline in 21 months, as domestic new orders softened and overseas export demand remained sluggish.
In contrast, the S&P Global Australia Services PMI Business Activity Index moderated to 51.4 in September from 53.2 in August, recording its fourth consecutive month of growth.
Reflecting the broader slowdown across both sectors, Australia’s Flash Composite PMI dropped to 50.8 in September from 52.7 in August, hitting its lowest reading since June.
Financial markets largely shrugged off the manufacturing downturn. The
rose 0.2% to 8,775 on Wednesday morning, extending prior gains. In currency markets, the Australian dollar traded near $0.71.

title: Australia Flash PMI: Manufacturing contracts for first time since March, services growth softens
